issue_snapshot.title: `pluggy` requires `from __future__ import annotations` although it shouldn't in Python 3.14
issue_snapshot.body:
This file is valid _in Python 3.14_, meaning, `python conftest.py` does not error:

`conftest.py`:
```python
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from _pytest.config import Config

def pytest_configure(config: Config) -> None: ...
```

In Python 3.13, it requires `from __future__ import annotations`.

Now, running `pytest` with the above `conftest.py` raises the following error. For some reason, `pluggy` seems to want to read the annotations and fails because `Config` is not available in non-type-checking mode.

Potential workarounds include:
- `Config` -> `"Config"` (but ruff undoes that)
- remove `if TYPE_CHECKING` (but ruff undoes that)
- add `from __future__ import annotations`

issue_snapshot.title: attrs doesn't recognize ClassVar if not imported in Python 3.14
issue_snapshot.body:
The following code

```python
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import attrs

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from typing import ClassVar

@attrs.define
class T:
    t: ClassVar[str]

T()
```

results in:
```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/test.py", line 12, in <module>
    T()
    ~^^
TypeError: T.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 't'
```

Since the `if TYPE_CHECKING` block doesn't run, `ClassVar` isn't defined and attrs can't evaluate the ForwardRef or doesn't recognize `ClassVar`:

```python
>>> attrs.fields_dict(T)["t"]
Attribute(name='t', default=NOTHING, validator=None, repr=True, eq=True, eq_key=None, order=True, order_key=None, hash=None, init=True, metadata=mappingproxy({}), type=ForwardRef('ClassVar[str]', is_class=True, owner=<class '__main__.T'>), converter=None, kw_only=False, inherited=False, on_setattr=None, alias='t')
```

Before Python 3.14, `T`'s definition would only run if you used a string annotation or `from __future__ import annotations` (which if used with 3.14, the above code runs fine), but with the new annotations behavior the class definition runs fine and this error appears. This is actually issue for dataclasses too, as I get the same error with them.

I'm not sure if this is fixable, but decided to report it, because it catches you by surprise

issue_snapshot.title: Tweak urllib3 version checker
issue_snapshot.body:
Hello,

Tiny corner case issue: building urllib3 on my side, I append a marker in the version string to distinguish theses builds, eg.: 2.6.3.build1

Would you consider a small change in requests and split the version string the same way it is done for chardet or charset normalizer ? It would prevent the check from failing on the `major, minor, patch = urllib3_version` line.

```diff
diff --git a/src/requests/__init__.py b/src/requests/__init__.py
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@ except ImportError:
 
 
 def check_compatibility(urllib3_version, chardet_version, charset_normalizer_version):
-    urllib3_version = urllib3_version.split(".")
+    urllib3_version = urllib3_version.split(".")[:3]
     assert urllib3_version != ["dev"]  # Verify urllib3 isn't installed from git.
 
     # Sometimes, urllib3 only reports its version as 16.1.
```

Regards.

issue_snapshot.title: [BUG] Double-free of wrk1/wrk2/iwrk in fitpack_surfit on allocation failure
issue_snapshot.body:
## Bug Description

In `scipy/interpolate/src/_fitpackmodule.c`, after the Fortran `surfit()` call, `wrk1`/`wrk2`/`iwrk` are freed but NOT set to NULL. If a subsequent `PyArray_SimpleNew` fails, `goto fail` frees them again.

## Location

`scipy/interpolate/src/_fitpackmodule.c:1578-1580, 1610-1618`

## Code

```c
free(wrk1);    // line 1578: freed
free(wrk2);    // line 1579: freed  
free(iwrk);    // line 1580: freed
// NOT set to NULL!

// ... if PyArray_SimpleNew fails later:
goto fail;

fail:
    free(wrk1);   // line 1610: DOUBLE FREE
    free(wrk2);   // line 1615: DOUBLE FREE
    free(iwrk);   // line 1618: DOUBLE FREE
```

## Impact

Double-free causes heap corruption. On modern allocators (glibc, jemalloc), this typically causes:
- Immediate crash (`double free detected`)
- Silent heap corruption leading to later crashes
- Potential security vulnerability (CWE-415)

Triggers when `PyArray_SimpleNew` fails due to OOM after the Fortran call.

## Suggested Fix

```c
free(wrk1); wrk1 = NULL;
free(wrk2); wrk2 = NULL;
free(iwrk); iwrk = NULL;
```

## Environment

- SciPy version: current main
- Affected: `scipy.interpolate.bisplrep` / surface fitting with OOM

issue_snapshot.title: ENH: implement a mask aware `np.unwrap` for masked arrays in the `np.ma` module
issue_snapshot.body:
### Proposed new feature or change:

In https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/31848 it was noticed that `unwrap` does not have a proper implementation for masked arrays. Currently the behavior is to completely unmask the array and return back an ndarray. The problem with that is that unwrap runs the loop over whatever garbage happen to be sitting in the masked slots as if it were real data which is wrong.

If we go calculate unwrap through the non-gufunc fallback instead, the mask survives, but diff/cumsum only know how to propagate masks positionally and they have no idea that unwrap needs the delta to the nearest valid sample. So a masked gap just gets treated as "no correction needed here," which can silently miss a real wrap and leave everything after the gap offset by a full period.

It should be possible to implement a proper mask-aware `np.ma.unwrap`. I have left a TODO in the code in that PR as a comment.

issue_snapshot.title: uv check --no-install-project
issue_snapshot.body:
### Summary

My project has extension modules that are heavy to build and require external non-Python dependencies. I do have *.pyi files for these extensions. I've setup `ty` such that I can install Python dependencies in .venv with `uv sync --no-install-project` and run `ty check` afterwards.

I would like to use `astral-sh/ty-pre-commit` hook, however I cannot figure out how to make it work without uv tying to install the project in  .venv. I'm guessing that `uv check` uses the `uv sync` machinery to setup/update .venv.

`uv check`  inherits most option related to extras/group installation from `uv sync`, but offers no control over the project installation. Therefore, IMHO it would make sense for `uv check` to accept a  `--no-install-project` flag just as `uv sync` does. 

### Example

```console
$ uv check --no-install-project ...
```
